raw_recipe.headline: Amy's Cilantro Cream Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This cilantro crema, or cream sauce, is spicy, light, and fragrant with cilantro. It is a refreshing dip or sauce for anything and everything.
raw_recipe.name: Amy's Cilantro Cream Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Combine cream cheese, tomatillo salsa, cilantro, sour cream, lime juice, garlic powder, pepper, celery salt, and cumin in a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth and creamy.

review.reviewBody: Cream cheese,cilantro and spices. How can you go wrong? I had no idea what a "bunch" of cilantro was precisely though; so I used about 1/2 cup (loosely packed)of fresh chopped; probably 20 pieces) Cilantro is a very strong, distinctive flavor and I probably could of used less. But, I love cilantro and I love med spicy salsas, so this is a dip that I will make again and again. I am just not sure if I like it best on "Southwestern Eggrolls" or for "Black Bean Pinwheels" best though... or maybe... on steak fajitas... or maybe on spicy-mesquite chicken tacos... Truly a fresh tasting, delicious dip for MANY different things! Just make sure you like the flavor of cilantro. Oh, FYI;this will be slightly "lumpy" if you do not have your cream cheese at room temperature. And, it will be AS spicy HOT AS THE BRAND YOU USE of tomatilla salsa (there are hundreds of different kinds;hot med, mild etc. just like any other salsa) Hope this helps you make it "5 star" for you... :)

Omg this is amazing!!! Instead of tomatillo sauce I used Serrano peppers and added two. I also added about an ounce or two of water to my blender because the cream cheese is too thick to blend. I suggest to put the water in first so it sit on the bottom of the blender so it's easier to blend. I ate it on our fish tacos and substituted tortilla with lettuce! This cilantro cream salsa is a must try!
The only thing I did was add 4 serrano peppers. It was a hit!

I needed to use some cilantro that was starting to wilt. I cut the recipe in half and decreased the amount of pepper. I didn't have salsa so I used about 1/2 cup of eggplant dip. It was amazingly good and I think easy to adapt to taste and use different ingredients (salsa of any kind, hummus, etc.) that you find in your fridge. I just served it with pita bread.

Some seem to be confused with the meaning of a bunch of cilantro. It’s exactly that, a pre-portioned amount at the grocery store tied together with a twisty tie. I used a little less since I’d already used some for another recipe. I also skipped the celery salt since I didn’t have any. I used the sauce on pan fried chicken that I seasoned well with salt and pepper. Also great with chips. It’s so delicious and creamy it’s easy to eat a lot! Thank you for such a versatile recipe!

This is so versatile! I made this for a grilled pork loin and we ended up using if for the pork loin and all the grilled veggies too. I only used 1/2 c. cilantro, I have no idea how you could use a whole bunch of cilantro. I feel that would be very overwhelming. I tasted the sauce before the cilantro went in and it would be good with out it, if you didn't like cilantro. I also used 1/2 tsp. celery seed and 1 tsp. salt in place of celery salt, since that's what I had. The cilantro flavor was much stronger the next day, almost too strong for my liking, so I would use it same day or add less cilantro if making it for next day. You could really use this for anything, veggie dip, bread dip, sandwich spread, sauce for meat or chips. It's really that good. Everyone at my dinner LOVED it!

I followed the recipe down to the cilantro, but didn’t have fresh, so I subbed 2 Tbsp dried. It was good, but I felt like it was missing something. I added another tablespoon of sour cream and lime juice, and an extra 1/2 tsp of cumin. Still wasn’t quite there to my taste, so I added about 2 Tbsp of honey—and there it was!

This is my new favorite dip I will make at every get together. I will put it on everything until I don’t have anything to dip and then will just eat it straight out of the bowl! I doubled the recipe really , except the cilantro...I felt one bunch was enough but that is just me. I also threw in a couple of avocados along with a pinch of jalapeño salt and it was yummy delicious. I made it for my bunco group and half the people used it as a salad dressing and half the people used it to sauce their chicken. Everyone loved it! Thank you Amy!.

I have been making this recipe for years! Very, very good as is as we LOVE cilantro. I do prefer less celery salt, and when the grocery store was out of tomatillo salsa one time, I made it with 2 small cans of green chilis and it was a yummy, milder version of the original. We eat it with enchiladas, tacos, fish, nachos, eggs, or pretty much anything! I also love it on a tofu buddha rice bowl as an alternative to a green curry dressing.

We enjoyed this sauce. We used it on spicy chicken tacos. I followed the recipe exactly. (Technically I did use low fat cream cheese) I felt it was just a smidge too salty. When I make it again, i will cut back to 1/2 tsp of celery salt. I can imagine using this as a base for a creamy cilantro salad dressing as well.

Delicious, better than restaurants. Probably because it is fresh. My son made it. Be sure to soften your cream cheese. Salsa choice makes much of the flavor and heat so pick one you like, as some tomatillo sauces in the jar are not so great. We love cilantro so used most of a moderate bunch. Subbed Greek fat free yogurt as we had no sour cream, used light cream cheese. I think better, fresher tasting than the heavier ingredients, but still very rich.
Couldn’t stop eating this. Goes with just about everything.Dip for chips, fresh veggies, on tacos, etc.thanks for sharing.
Made this exactly as written. Fantastic on southwest burritos,but would be great on anything.
Made this to use on some shrimp tempura tacos, tasted amazing! I used chive and onion cream cheese and I think it elevated the flavor. Will be making it again :)
Great flavor. Going to be perfect for on fish fillets. I didn't have any tomatillo salsa, so I used and equal sized can of fire roasted dices green chilies. Ready to make and delicious!
We won’t eat tacos without this. It’s absolutely delicious! We have been making it for years!

I was trying to recreate a pasta salad with cilantro cream sauce from a Columbus restaurant. It was way too peppery - enough to catch you in the back of the throat. I don't usually start tweaking recipes, but I will have to for this. I was looking for a smooth, slightly sweet cilantro cream sauce. So, I'll be adding some honey, cutting the pepper back to half the amount, and I added 1/2 cup of sour cream to try and cut the taste. Also, the "bunch" of cilantro is not precise enough - the bunches by me are quite large, so going down to 1/2 a bunch. But it's a starting point - thanks.
this is very good for a change of pace
Very good. The entire family enjoyed.
